industry: Defense Prime Contractor / Aerospace and Space Systems
thesis: Northrop Grumman is a top-tier U.S. defense prime with unmatched positions in strategic deterrence (B-21 Raider bomber, Sentinel ICBM), space systems, and missile defense. A record backlog above $95B, 26% free-cash-flow growth in FY2025, and rising demand from Golden Dome missile-defense architecture and NATO rearmament underpin a BUY rating, with margin recovery and B-21 production ramp as the key upside levers.

drivers: B-21 Raider transitions to full-rate production with improving fixed-price margins
Golden Dome homeland missile-defense architecture drives multi-billion-dollar Space and Mission Systems awards
Sentinel ICBM program restructuring stabilizes and re-baselines to profitable execution
NATO and allied rearmament sustains record munitions, radar, and space bookings
Free cash flow compounds toward $4B-plus, funding accelerated buybacks and dividend growth

base_case.assumptions: Low-to-mid single-digit organic revenue growth in line with 2026 guidance of $43.5B–$44B, segment operating margin recovering back toward 11%, backlog held above $90B, and the stock trading at roughly 19–20x forward EPS consistent with large-cap defense-prime multiples.

risks: Additional fixed-price charges on B-21, Sentinel, or guided-missile programs compress margins
U.S. deficit-reduction pressure or a continuing resolution slows defense outlays and new awards
Sentinel cost growth triggers further Nunn-McCurdy scrutiny or program restructuring
Space Systems growth decelerates as legacy launch and satellite programs wind down
Multiple compression toward 16–17x forward EPS on earnings or backlog stagnation

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 Earnings — margin recovery and B-21 production progress
FY2027 Defense Budget Request and NDAA — strategic-deterrence and Golden Dome funding visibility
B-21 Raider low-rate to full-rate production decision
Golden Dome missile-defense architecture award decisions
Q4 and Full-Year 2026 Earnings — backlog, FCF, and 2027 guidance

key_risks: Fixed-price development contract cost overruns on B-21, Sentinel, and guided-missile programs
U.S. defense budget volatility, continuing resolutions, or deficit-driven spending cuts
Concentration risk with roughly 84% of revenue from the U.S. government
Sentinel ICBM cost growth and Nunn-McCurdy restructuring execution risk
Supply-chain inflation and skilled-labor constraints pressuring margins and schedules
